raw.description: Hardcoded secret key for JWT token signing.
raw.exploit: An attacker with access to the source code can use the hardcoded secret key to forge JWT tokens.
An attacker with access to the source code can use the hardcoded credentials to access the database.

raw.description: No CSRF protection on state-changing endpoints.
raw.exploit: An attacker can trick a user into making unwanted requests to the server by exploiting the lack of CSRF protection.
An attacker can use error messages to gain information about the system, such as the existence of certain users.

raw.description: Lack of role-based access control for file upload and download.
raw.exploit: An attacker can exploit this to upload or download files they should not have access to.

raw.description: Potential SSRF vulnerability in file download functionality.
raw.exploit: An attacker can manipulate the file path to access internal resources.

raw.description: Lack of output encoding for file names.
raw.exploit: An attacker can upload a file with a name containing HTML/JavaScript code, potentially leading to XSS when the file name is displayed.
